questions.q: What is the stated purpose of the continual improvement practice in ITIL 4?
options: To align the organization's practices and services with changing business needs, through the ongoing identification and improvement of services, components, or practices
To approve or reject proposed changes before deployment
To track the financial lifecycle of IT assets
To resolve a single incident and close its ticket
questions.explain: The key word in the purpose statement is 'ongoing' -- it's a standing capability, not a one-time project.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct first step of the ITIL Continual Improvement Model?
options: Take action
What is the vision?
Did we get there?
How do we keep the momentum going?
questions.explain: The model starts by understanding the high-level business objective driving the improvement, before assessing the current state.

questions.q: Why does the Continual Improvement Model loop its final step back into its first step?
options: Because the model is actually a one-time checklist with seven boxes to tick
Because reinforcing what worked feeds directly into identifying the next vision, making it a repeatable cycle rather than a finished project
Because step seven and step one are actually the same step, listed twice
The model does not loop; it ends permanently after step seven
questions.explain: The loop back to 'what is the vision?' is exactly what makes this a continual, repeatable model instead of a single improvement effort.

questions.q: According to this lesson, whose job is continual improvement meant to be?
options: A dedicated continual improvement team working quietly in the background
Only senior leadership setting annual improvement targets
Only the problem management practice, since it already looks for patterns
Everyone's -- embedded into daily work rather than handled as a separate team's occasional initiative
questions.explain: ITIL 4 is explicit that this practice is meant to be embedded into everyone's daily work, not isolated to a specialist team.

questions.q: Which Service Value Chain activity does the continual improvement practice put into concrete, daily action?
options: Engage
Improve
Obtain/Build
Design & Transition
questions.explain: Chapter 3's 'Improve' value chain activity exists to keep every other activity getting better over time; this practice is how that actually happens day to day.
